newsItems.headline: Traders see September rate hike as European Central Bank mulls energy price spike
Dollar hits new 40-year high versus yen, euro lower after ECB decision - Reuters

briefing.briefing: Right now, the most relevant forces pushing and pulling gold are a rising US dollar, climbing bond yields [the interest rate the US government pays on its debt — higher yields make gold less attractive since gold pays no interest], and a Federal Reserve that markets are 100% certain will hold rates steady at their July 29th meeting. The dollar strength story has been turbocharged by news out of Europe: about 18 hours ago Reuters reported the dollar hit a 40-year high against the Japanese yen with the euro also falling, and then roughly 5-6 hours ago CNBC flagged that traders are now pricing in a possible ECB [European Central Bank] rate hike in September due to an energy price spike — a hike would normally support the euro, but the headline seems to be creating noise rather than clarity, with the dollar remaining firm. A strong dollar is generally bad for gold because gold is priced in dollars — when the dollar rises, gold becomes more expensive for foreign buyers and tends to fall. Despite gold trading at a lofty $4,048, here is the critical piece of data: the 14-day Average Daily Range [the typical daily price swing] is 86.5 points, but today's range has already used 100.8 points — meaning the market has moved MORE than its average daily distance already. That strongly suggests today's directional momentum is largely exhausted and we are likely entering choppy, directionless price action for the remainder of this session. Real yields [bond yields adjusted for inflation] ticked up slightly today, another mild headwind for gold. GLD ETF flows are flat over three weeks and large traders reduced their net long positions by over 7,000 contracts in the latest report, suggesting waning bullish conviction. Confidence in any directional bias is just 4/10 — the main reason to stay cautious is that today's calendar is completely empty of scheduled news events, so there is no fresh catalyst likely to create a clean trending move. What would change this view: a sharp reversal in the dollar, a surprise geopolitical escalation, or gold reclaiming and holding above today's high. For a trend-following trader, this is NOT a good window for new trades — the daily range is used up, the dollar is strong, and there is no fresh news catalyst to drive a clean move. If you must trade, keep size very small and wait for a proper 1H structure shift [a clear change in the direction of price on the hourly chart] before committing. The golden rule for today: when the daily range is already exceeded, patient hands beat trigger-happy ones.
